They are trained to be calm and collected, and again, to simultaneously dispatch the help you need while talking you through what you should be doing. An EMT isn't going to be better at this, a police officer isn't going to be better at this, and a firefighter isn't going to be better at this, because the dispatcher isn't just making stuff up on the fly, they're giving advice based on guidelines that were developed by experts in each field, without letting their personal opinions get in the way.

Also, its a poor argument that the extra 2 seconds it takes to describe your emergency is going to make a difference, considering that you're going to have to do that no matter who you call. In the US, you can call EMS and police directly, but guess what, it would be slower than just calling 911. The dispatchers send out the first units as soon as they have your location and the emergency (so, basically, the 1st 20 seconds of the call), and then update the responders or upgrade the call while everyone is on the way.
